nodes.question: What have many countries and organizations developed in response to human impacts on the planet?
nodes.answer: They have developed approaches and policies to alleviate human impacts on planet Earth.
nodes.paragraph: Through violence and other forms of erasure, the latter rose as the prevalent worldview, installing the individualistic ethics of Western thinking and doing, focused on advancing agendas to colonize nature and mechanize ecosystems for human society. As a result, the last century has been termed the Anthropocene, the Era of Humanity , which is presently being challenged across the globe by ecological crises. * Valoree Gagnon vsgagnon@mtu.edu 1 College of Forest Resources and Environmental Science, Michigan Technological University, Room 168, U.J. Noblet Forestry Bldg, Houghton, MI 49931, USA 2 Department of Humanities, Michigan Technological University, Houghton, MI 49931, USA 3 Department of Social Sciences, Michigan Technological University, Houghton, MI 49931, USA 4 Natural Resources Department, Keweenaw Bay Indian Community, Baraga, MI 49908, USA 44 Socio-Ecological Practice Research (2025) 7:43 55 In response, many countries and organizations have devel- oped approaches and policies to alleviate human impacts on planet Earth. nodes.question: What is the primary focus of the analytical approach discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The primary focus is on designing more effective public policies to strengthen resilience and mitigate the effects of climate disasters on food security.
nodes.paragraph: This approach provides a robust analytical tool for designing more effective public policies that strengthen resilience and mitigate the effects of climate disasters on food security. 1 3 Economic and Food Security Impacts of Climate Disasters and Mitigation The remainder of the paper is organized as follows: Sect. 2 describes the data and the methodological framework. Section 3 discusses the simulations and results. Section 4 out- lines the policy implications of the findings and Sect. 5 concludes the paper. 2 Data and Methodological Framework The methodological framework uses a top-down macro-micro modeling approach to deter - mine the changes in the economy and food security due to climate disasters in Nigeria. We use a dynamic general equilibrium model (CGE) in the macroeconomic component. Then, the macro-simulation results are broken down at the household level by rural or urban areas and regions in a microsimulation module. The micro model is used to assess the impact of climate shocks on consumption, food security, and food poverty. 2.1 Data Sources The data for the CGE model is the 2019 Social Accounting Matrix (SAM) constructed by Mitik et al.
